newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Soccer-Bosman charity match likely in Brussels.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Bosman charity match likely in Brussels.

text.p: A charity match in aid of Belgian Jean-Marc Bosman which had been repeatedly blocked by soccer authorities in the past year is now likely to be played in Brussels, the International soccer Players' Union (AIFP) said on Monday.

"I cannot confirm as yet...but it is very likely it will be in Brussels," AIFP Secretary-General Didier Roustan told reporters after the union's first meeting with European Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn.
He was unable to give a date or further details on the game.
Bosman's case in the European Court of Justice brought about the end of quotas on foreign players in Europe, but also left the player financially stranded after a five-year legal fight.

Last year, Bosman attacked the sport's world governing body FIFA over alleged attempts to block the organisation of a benefit match in Paris and efforts to have it staged in Barcelona on April 27 were vetoed by the Spanish federation.

AIFP, which was represented at the meeting with Flynn by Manchester United's Frenchman Eric Cantona, PSG's Brazilian Rai and Belgian Georges Grun of Reggiana, will still organise a Europe-Rest of the World game in Barcelona on April 27.
A second game will be for Bosman and a third in support of the European year against racism, Roustan said. Cantona confirmed he would be "very proud" to play the anti-racism game.
Cantona said soccer was "at a turning point" now that the Bosman ruling had been accepted by soccer authorities.
He said that now more and more soccer-related cases were brought to court.

"We feel that we're going to have a need for some sort of legal framework. This is going to come in the near future, laws will be created and we would like to fully participate in that process of creating laws," he said.
Flynn said the players had immediately shown their concern and expressed their support for the European year against racism.
"I hadn't expected such a generous response," he said.
He said that AIFP wanted to be involved in soccer-related issues at the highest level.
"They want to be consulted and they want to have a say in how a game is organised in the best interest of the game," he said.
"We've agreed that this will not be the only occasion to meet to discuss further possibilities in so far as the progress of football is concerned," he said.
Dutch Euro MP Jimmy Janssen van Raay said he had always supported the idea of an international trade union of players.
"That way players with a world-wide fame could take care of lesser-known colleagues," he said.
